READABILITY.evidence: Names state their purpose (shapeIndexDecoder, readCount, decodeCell, maxDecodeCapacity). Public Encode/Decode have doc comments, and the non-obvious parts are commented. Short names like e, d, p, l follow Go receiver/helper idiom.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Ignores the convention to put per-shape encode/decode beside each type and to reuse typeTag. It adds its own shapeIndexShapeTag enum and one big type switch in shapeindex_encode.go. It also changes applyUpdatesInternal so every update rebuilds the whole index, which is scope creep.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Every count is capped by readCount before allocating, and slice capacity is limited by maxDecodeCapacity. Cell order, shape IDs, edge IDs and finite coordinates are all checked. Errors go through the sticky d.err, and the index is left unchanged on failure. The recover() guard is a backstop and returns an error.

C7-14-CASE1.evidence: Adds ShapeIndex.Encode/Decode only. Existing per-shape Encode/Decode, typeTag values and the Shape interface are untouched. It uses a private shapeIndexShapeTag enum, so existing wire formats are not affected.
